audit_metadata.method: Static, read-only code/doc/git audit. No application code was modified. Evidence gathered by direct file reads, ripgrep-based search, git history inspection, and five parallel read-only sub-audits (databases/queues/scheduler/websockets; agents/models/prompts; risk/backtesting/paper/live-execution; security/reliability/tech-debt; tests/integrations/decision-pipeline). No code was executed except read-only 'pytest --collect-only' and a prior full regression run performed for an unrelated task in this same session.

repository_metadata.name: TradingAgents (git remote name: trading-workstation)
repository_metadata.description: Single-user, local-first paper-trading research workstation and market-intelligence platform for Indian (NSE/BSE) and select US equities. Two largely separate pipelines: (1) a human-approval paper-trading execution path (live/, paper/, risk/, strategy/baseline.py), and (2) a market-intelligence/recommendation pipeline (market_data/, market_intelligence/, research/, decision_engine/, predictions/, learning/) that never touches execution. A third, independent layer (quant_research/, backtesting/, strategy/*) runs offline statistical hypothesis research and is not wired into either live pipeline.
repository_metadata.dependency_manifest: requirements.txt (42 lines) -- direct-dependency contract, not a full pip freeze

documentation.note: Development proceeded in 45+ numbered phases (Phase 0 through post-Phase-42 bridge/critic work), each phase self-documented with an evidence-labeled report. Phases 1-7 (and one Phase-15-adjacent audit) exist only as externally-hosted Claude Artifacts, never committed to the repo -- a disclosed documentation gap.

git_state.branch_count_note: 150+ local/remote branches exist (one per phase and per feature/fix, e.g. phase-16-dhan-connectivity, feature-deterministic-critic-core, fix-stale-pending-order-bypasses-risk-halt), almost none deleted after merge -- see technical_debt entry 'stale-branch-accumulation'.

services.name: Scheduler (schedule tick / schedule loop)

evidence.description: Runs at most one due slot then exits -- designed to be invoked by an EXTERNAL scheduler (cron/Task Scheduler), which this repo does not itself configure.
A plain Python while-loop with time.sleep(interval) between ticks -- not an OS-level daemon/cron; only runs as long as this one foreground/background process stays alive.
BEGIN IMMEDIATE-based atomic lock preventing overlapping runs; reclaim_stale_locks() (line 130) recovers from a crashed process.

risks: No OS-level scheduling exists anywhere in the repo -- 'continuous operation' depends entirely on an operator (or an external supervisor not present in this repo) keeping 'schedule loop' running.

Currently NOT running in this environment -- see project_scheduler memory / data/scheduler_runs.db, last activity stale, root cause previously diagnosed as missing Dhan credentials in this environment.
services.next_action: If continuous unattended operation is required, wire 'schedule loop' (or repeated 'schedule tick') into an OS-level process supervisor -- none exists today.
